extraction.name: OWSM v4: Improving Open Whisper-Style Speech Models via Data Scaling and Cleaning
extraction.description: A cleaned version of the YODAS speech dataset created with a scalable data-cleaning pipeline, yielding 166,000 hours of speech across 75 languages, used alongside existing OWSM data to train OWSM v4 models.
extraction.creator: Yifan Peng, Muhammad Shakeel, Yui Sudo, William Chen, Jinchuan Tian, Chyi-Jiunn Lin, Shinji Watanabe
extraction.citeAs: Yifan Peng, Muhammad Shakeel, Yui Sudo, William Chen, Jinchuan Tian, Chyi-Jiunn Lin, Shinji Watanabe. "OWSM v4: Improving Open Whisper-Style Speech Models via Data Scaling and Cleaning." Interspeech 2025. DOI: 10.21437/Interspeech.2025-1062.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was built by applying a three-step cleaning pipeline to raw YODAS web-crawled long-form recordings: resegmenting and realigning audio-text pairs with CTC segmentation, filtering utterances by language identification agreement between original labels and predictions from text and audio, and filtering low-quality alignments using CTC confidence scores.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data came from YODAS, which contains web-crawled, unsegmented long-form audio recordings with text transcriptions and timestamps.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: After realignment, long-form recordings were segmented into utterances up to 30 seconds, non-speech-only utterances were removed, language labels were validated using text and audio LID, and utterances were filtered by language-specific CTC-score quantiles with a chosen threshold of 0.10.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Preprocessing included CTC-based audio-text realignment, segmentation of long-form audio into short utterances of at most 30 seconds, removal of non-speech segments, LID-based filtering, and CTC-score-based filtering.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The raw YODAS recordings were accompanied by text transcriptions annotated with start and end timestamps; the paper additionally describes original language labels that were checked against predicted labels from text and audio.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The authors analyzed annotation quality by identifying mismatched language labels and audio-text misalignments, and used CTC confidence scores to quantify alignment quality and filter low-quality data.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: OWSM-CTC v3.2, fastText language identification model, SpeechBrain ECAPA-TDNN spoken LID model, CTC segmentation algorithm
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors state they will publicly release the cleaned YODAS data, data-cleaning pipeline/scripts, training code, pre-trained models, and logs via ESPnet; the paper also notes that future versions of YODAS can grow.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The work is positioned as advancing open academic research and addressing concerns about privacy, transparency, and reproducibility associated with closed training data.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The cleaned dataset remains highly imbalanced across languages, with English dominating and many languages underrepresented; the authors keep the original distribution without resampling.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Raw YODAS contains annotation errors including incorrect language labels and audio-text misalignments; the cleaned dataset still has highly imbalanced language distribution, and the OWSM-CTC model used for resegmentation supports only a subset of YODAS languages.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and fine-tuning speech foundation models for automatic speech recognition, language identification, and speech translation; the cleaned YODAS data was used alongside previous OWSM data to train OWSM v4 models and to fine-tune a pre-trained OWSM v3.1 model for threshold selection.

name.evidence: OWSM v4: Improving Open Whisper-Style Speech Models via Data Scaling and Cleaning

description.evidence: To address this, we develop a scalable data-cleaning pipeline using public toolkits, yielding a dataset with 166,000 hours of speech across 75 languages. Our new series of OWSM v4 models, trained on this curated dataset alongside existing OWSM data, significantly outperform previous versions on multilingual benchmarks.

license.evidence: This work enhances OWSM by integrating YODAS, a large-scale web-crawled dataset with a Creative Commons license.

creator.evidence: Yifan Peng1, Muhammad Shakeel2, Yui Sudo2, William Chen1, Jinchuan Tian1, Chyi-Jiunn Lin1, Shinji Watanabe1

isLiveDataset.evidence: The current version already includes 370k hours of audio in 149 languages. Future versions can further grow.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: Figure 1 illustrates our data-cleaning pipeline consisting of the following three steps. ... our first step is to realign the audio and text using the CTC segmentation algorithm [31]. ... We retain only those utterances for which the original language label matches both the predicted language from the text and the predicted language from the audio. ... The final step removes utterances with low-quality audio-text alignments, as indicated by the CTC score calculated in Section 2.1.1.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: YODAS is a large-scale web-crawled dataset with a Creative Commons license. ... YODAS establishes a scalable pipeline to crawl data from the web.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: YODAS provides unsegmented long-form recordings, each of them is accompanied by a list of text transcriptions annotated with start and end timestamps.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: Following realignment, the long-form audio recordings are segmented into shorter utterances, each with a maximum duration of 30 seconds. Utterances that consist exclusively of non-speech elements, such as music, are removed. ... We retain only those utterances for which the original language label matches both the predicted language from the text and the predicted language from the audio. ... we opt for a threshold of θCTC = 0.10.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: YODAS provides unsegmented long-form recordings, each of them is accompanied by a list of text transcriptions annotated with start and end timestamps. ... We observe that certain utterances have incorrect language labels.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: Common issues include mismatched language labels and misalignment between audio and text. ... after CTC segmentation, each short utterance is assigned a confidence score, which quantifies the alignment quality between the audio and the corresponding text. This confidence score is subsequently utilized to filter low-quality data

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: we employ the publicly available OWSM-CTC v3.2 model ... using the CTC segmentation algorithm [31]. ... Specifically, the text-based LID model is sourced from fastText [32, 33], while the spoken LID model is based on ECAPA-TDNN, developed by SpeechBrain [34].

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: We will publicly release the cleaned YODAS data, pre-trained models, and all associated scripts via the ESPnet toolkit. ... To advance open academic research, we will publicly release our data-cleaning scripts, the curated YODAS dataset, training code, pre-trained models, and training logs. ... Future versions can further grow.

rai:personalSensitiveInformation.evidence: Common issues include mismatched language labels ... We observe that certain utterances have incorrect language labels.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: However, Whisper does not publicly release its training data, code, and logs, leading to concerns about privacy, transparency, and reproducibility. To advance open research, researchers from academic institutions have developed a series of fully open Whisper-style speech models (OWSM)

rai:dataBiases.evidence: Similar to the raw YODAS data, the distribution across languages is highly imbalanced. English constitutes the largest share, whereas many other languages continue to be underrepresented. For simplicity, in this work, we keep the original distribution without any resampling.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: The raw YODAS data has not undergone a rigorous cleaning process and may contain annotation errors [24]. Common issues include mismatched language labels and misalignment between audio and text. ... we employ the publicly available OWSM-CTC v3.2 model, which supports only a subset of the languages present in YODAS. ... the distribution across languages is highly imbalanced.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: Our new series of OWSM v4 models, trained on this curated dataset alongside existing OWSM data ... To identify a suitable threshold, we fine-tune a pre-trained small-sized OWSM v3.1 (367M) [14] on the cleaned YODAS data filtered at different thresholds. ... We develop a new series of OWSM v4 models ... trained on the cleaned YODAS dataset in conjunction with previous OWSM data
